cues.text: Start with the simplest picture there is. A factory. Nell's factory.
Every month, money comes in. Customers buy what she makes, and they pay her.
Economists call that money coming in her revenue. Revenue is all the money coming in, before anything is taken out of it.
Every month, money also goes out. She pays for materials, for electricity, for wages, for the rent.
That is her cost. All the money going out to keep the place running.
The difference between the two is what she actually keeps.
Her profit. Revenue minus cost. What is left over.
Not all costs behave the same way. The rent is the same whether she makes one chair or a thousand.
fixed cost. A cost that does not change with how much you make.
The wood is different. Make twice as many chairs and she buys twice as much wood.
variable cost. A cost that rises and falls with how much you make.
Now the word this whole film turns on.
You may think investment means buying shares in a company. That is not what an economist means by it.
It means this. You spend a large sum of money now, to build something that will produce revenue later.
Investment. Spending a large sum now, to build something that produces revenue later.
A factory. A shop fitted out. A well drilled. A machine bought. That is investment, and that is the decision this whole film is about.
